chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, when he entered the privy, would cover his head and say to himself:

In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and there is no god but Allah. My Lord, remove the harm from me freely without reckoning, and make me among those grateful to You for what You turn away from me of harm and distress, which, had You withheld it from me, I would have perished. To You belongs all praise. Protect me from the evil of what is in this place, bring me out of it safe, and place a barrier between me and obedience to the accursed Satan.

key_terms.الشَّاكِرِينَ: those who are grateful to Allah
key_terms.الْأَذَى: harm or noxious matter being removed
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: beginning with the Name of Allah

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام recite when entering the restroom?
ai.summary: This hadith records a supplication of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام when entering the place of relieving oneself. It combines remembrance of Allah, gratitude for relief from bodily harm, and seeking protection from evil and from obeying al-Shayṭān al-Rajīm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.41 - When Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) would enter the restroom, he would cover his head and say privately:

Bismillahi wa billahi wa la ilaha illa Allah, Rabb akhrij ‘anni al-adha sarhan bighayri hisabin, wa aj‘alni laka mina ash-shakireena fima tAsrifuhu ‘anni minal-adha wa al-ghammi alladhi law habastahu ‘anni halaktu. Laka al-hamdu, i‘simni min sharri ma fi hadhihi al-buq‘ah, wa akhrijni minha saliman, wa hul bayni wa bayna ta‘ati ash-shaytan ar-rajeem
"In the name of Allah (swt) and by Allah (swt). There is no god but Allah (swt). O’ Lord (azj), remove harm from me completely without difficulty, and make me among those who are grateful for the relief You grant me from harm and distress, which, if You withheld, would cause my destruction. Praise be to You. Protect me from the evil of what may be in this place, and let me leave safely. Place a barrier between me and obedience to the accursed devil."
